reproduction_target: Two chained computational targets on the Iowa Mungbean Diversity (IMD) panel (372 genotypes, 2022-23 field trials, 2,418 flatbed-scanned pod images). (1) A Python/PyTorch AI image-phenotyping pipeline: Tesseract OCR metadata tag reading, U-Net(ResNet34) pod detection/cropping, DeepLabV3(ResNet34) pod-background segmentation, geometric trait extraction (calibration 0.00847 cm/px, skeletonized midline length, 100-point width sampling, RMSE straightness-index curvature), and a 5-checkpoint U-Net ensemble for seed-per-pod counting. (2) An R/Python quantitative-genetics stack on the extracted phenotypes plus 13,414 filtered GBS SNPs: descriptive statistics and Box-Cox/outlier handling, BLUEs and Cullis broad-sense heritability via the R inti package, LD decay in TASSEL v5.0 with a Hill-Weir NLS fit, STRUCTURE v2.3.4 population structure with STRUCTURE HARVESTER and CLUMPAK, phenotypic PCA in scikit-learn 1.3.0, four GWAS models (MLM/FarmCPU/BLINK via GAPIT v3, plus SVEN), Manhattan/Q-Q plotting (ggplot2/ggrepel/ggpubr/qqman), candidate-gene identification via Legume Information System JBrowse + BLASTP against soybean/cowpea/common bean/TAIR at E<=1e-20, a SequenceServer v3.1.2 (BLASTP 2.15.0) synteny chord diagram, and rrBLUP genomic prediction under 10-fold cross-validation. Field trials, harvesting, flatbed image acquisition, manual pod measurement and manual seed annotation are wet-lab/physical (W, out of scope for computational reproduction).
granularity_note: Coarse one-step-per-named-tool/analysis, extracted from the bioRxiv JATS XML source (fetched by curl after WebFetch returned HTTP 403) plus the GitHub landing page and README prose only. No workflow file exists; there is no Snakefile/Nextflow/Makefile. 17 computational steps are verdicted; 5 wet-lab/physical steps (field RCBD trial 2022-23, R6 harvest and pod bagging, Epson Expression 11000 XL scanning at 300 dpi, manual pod length/seed-count/curvature scoring, manual seed annotation in Microsoft Paint and LabelMe training annotation) are counted in W and not verdicted, per the sibling-report convention. A material asymmetry drives most of the scoring: the Data Availability statement claims 'All analysis scripts used in this study are publicly available at GitHub', but the repository landing page lists only 8 blobs (7 R/Rmd scripts + README) and contains NO Python, no model definitions, and no trained weights for the U-Net/DeepLabV3/OCR image pipeline that produces the paper's headline phenotypes. Separately, the README describes a revised version of the study (T2T 'Weilv-9' reference genome, 65 significant SNPs, candidate genes on chromosomes 4 and 6, conditionally accepted in G3) that does not match this preprint (45 significant SNPs, candidate genes on chromosomes 1 and 2, LIS accession VC1973A.gnm7.SB53); the README also points GWAS/GP inputs at 'the genotypic dataset (available on Figshare)' with no Figshare DOI or URL anywhere in either document. Version pins are prose-only and partial: Python 3.10, PyTorch 1.13, Tesseract v5.3.0, TASSEL v5.0, STRUCTURE v2.3.4, GAPIT v3, scikit-learn 1.3.0, SequenceServer v3.1.2, BLASTP 2.15.0 in the paper; R >= 4.2.0 with GAPIT3 v3.1.0, rrBLUP v4.6.1, sommer v4.3.3, lme4 v1.1-34, data.table v1.14.8, ggplot2 v3.4.2, dplyr v1.1.2 in the README. No lockfile, container, conda env, requirements.txt, release or tag exists in the repository, so version is capped at 1 everywhere it is pinned at all.

steps.label: OCR metadata tag identification — region binarization, largest-connected-component tag isolation, Tesseract v5.3.0 with a restricted character set, regex validation of Plot/PI identifiers, cropped tags saved for traceability

Pod detection and cropping — U-Net with ResNet34 encoder (segmentation_models_pytorch) trained on LabelMe annotations, 20 largest components sorted bottom-left to top-right, bounding-box crops per pod

Pod-background segmentation — DeepLabV3 with ResNet34 backbone per cropped pod, largest-connected-component retention, unspecified morphological refinement, three outputs per pod (binary mask, overlay, trait-ready mask)

Geometric trait extraction — pixel-to-cm calibration (1 px = 0.00847 cm, n = 50 scans), midline skeletonization by topmost/bottommost contour midpoints, length in cm, width from 100 sampled midline points (mean/max/median), curvature as RMSE of a regression line fitted to the midline
Seed-per-pod estimation — U-Net (ResNet34 encoder) seed segmentation, ensemble of 5 checkpoints (epochs 5-9) with output averaging, thresholded segmentation, connected-component counting

Descriptive statistics of pod traits — per-genotype averaging over 20 pods, normality inspection with Box-Cox transformation 'where necessary', +/-3 SD outlier removal, Pearson correlations visualized with the R corrplot package (repo script 01_descriptive_statistics.R)

BLUEs/BLUPs and broad-sense heritability — multi-environment linear mixed model (environment and genotype fixed, block-within-environment and genotype-by-environment random) and Cullis et al. (2006) H2 via the R inti package (repo script 03_trait_blups.Rmd)

Genome-wide LD analysis — TASSEL v5.0 pairwise r2 on 13,414 HapMap SNPs, 50-SNP sliding window, MAF 0.05, Hill-Weir (1988)/Remington (2001) non-linear model fitted by NLS regression, half-decay distance, plotted in R

Population structure — STRUCTURE v2.3.4 admixture model with correlated allele frequencies on 13,414 SNPs, K = 2-10, 5 independent runs per K, 10,000 burn-in and 100,000 MCMC replicates, optimal K by Evanno delta-K in STRUCTURE HARVESTER, run alignment via CLUMPAK

Phenotypic PCA — seven pod traits (image + manual BLUEs, 372 genotypes), column-mean imputation, z-standardization, SVD, eigenvalue > 1 retention, loadings and biplot, using scikit-learn 1.3.0 in Python

SNP filtering and covariate construction — 19,658 -> 13,414 SNPs after removing sites with >15% missing data and MAF < 0.05; kinship (K) matrix and first three principal components computed in TASSEL as GWAS covariates

GWAS with GAPIT version 3 — single-locus MLM plus multi-locus FarmCPU and BLINK on BLUEs from manual and image-based phenotypes, K matrix + 3 PCs as covariates, Bonferroni threshold -log10(0.05/n) (repo script 04_gwas_gapit_pipeline.Rmd)

GWAS with SVEN (Selection of Variables with Embedded screening using Bayesian methods; Li et al. 2023) — no package version, no prior specification, no MCMC/screening settings, no RNG seed given (repo script 05_gwas_sven_method.R)

GWAS result visualization — Manhattan plots for MLM/FarmCPU/BLINK using ggplot2 (v3.4.2 per README), ggrepel and ggpubr; Q-Q plots with qqman; Venn diagram of model overlap (repo script s02_venn_diagram_figS2.R)

Candidate gene identification and comparative mapping — interactive Legume Information System JBrowse/ZZBrowse/Genome Context Viewer/Gene Family Search gene lookup inside the LD block, BLASTP of candidate proteins against Glycine max, Vigna unguiculata and Phaseolus vulgaris in LIS and against Arabidopsis in TAIR at E-value cutoff 1e-20
Synteny chord diagram across mungbean, soybean, cowpea and common bean proteins — generated on the hosted SequenceServer version 3.1.2 using BLASTP 2.15.0 at sequenceserver.legumeinfo.org

Genomic prediction — rrBLUP ridge-regression BLUP (v4.6.1 per README) on the 13,414-marker matrix against manual and image-based BLUPs, ten-fold cross-validation with identical fold partitions across phenotyping methods, per-fold MAF >= 0.05 and zero-variance marker exclusion, Pearson r / R2 / MSE / bias averaged over folds, top-10 selection-coincidence index (repo script 06_rrblup_genomic_prediction.R)

headline.static_readiness: 0/17 (0%) — stage1 ceiling only, no R★ (R★ needs stage-2 code verification). Unexecuted; no declared environment closure exists to be statically validated, and n_exact_capture_unexecuted = 0, n_fetch_required = 0.
headline.inference_inclusive_upper_bound: RI ceiling on 9/17 computational steps (C6, C7, C8, C9, C10, C11, C12, C14, C17) — the R/TASSEL/STRUCTURE/scikit-learn quantitative-genetics half of the study, where the phenotype and genotype inputs are public, parameters are stated in unusual detail, and at least a partial version pin exists in the paper or the README. The remaining 8/17 cap at NI for two distinct reasons. (a) The entire AI image pipeline (C1-C5), which produces the paper's headline phenotypes, has data = 0: the 2,418 scanned pod images, the LabelMe pod-segmentation annotations and the Microsoft Paint seed annotations are nowhere deposited, and C2/C3/C5 additionally have code = 0 because no Python source and no trained model weights are in the cited repository despite the blanket claim that 'All analysis scripts used in this study are publicly available at GitHub'. (b) C13 (SVEN) names no version and no prior/MCMC/seed settings; C15 and C16 are interactive hosted web-service analyses (LIS JBrowse, TAIR BLAST, SequenceServer) with no script and no database snapshot date. No lockfile, container digest or conda spec is claimed anywhere, so even under stage 2 no step can exceed RI on environment grounds. The single largest lever would be depositing the images plus the Python/PyTorch pipeline and weights, which would move 5 NI steps toward RI.
headline.coverage: 17 computational steps assessed from the bioRxiv v1 JATS-XML Methods prose plus the GitHub repository landing page and README prose only; no code was read line-by-line and nothing was executed. 5 wet-lab/physical steps (2022-23 RCBD field trials at Iowa State AEA/Burkey/Bruner farms, R6-stage harvest and pod bagging, Epson Expression 11000 XL flatbed scanning at 300 dpi, manual pod length/seed-count/curvature phenotyping, manual seed annotation of 1,678 images in Microsoft Paint and LabelMe training annotation) are counted in W and are out of computational-reproduction scope.

gaps.where: AI image-phenotyping pipeline (steps C1-C5) vs. the cited repository github.com/vboddepalli89/Image-based-pod-phenotyping
gaps.missing: The Data Availability statement asserts 'All analysis scripts used in this study are publicly available at GitHub', but the repository contains only 8 blobs — 01_descriptive_statistics.R, 02_methods_comparison_fig2.Rmd, 03_trait_blups.Rmd, 04_gwas_gapit_pipeline.Rmd, 05_gwas_sven_method.R, 06_rrblup_genomic_prediction.R, s02_venn_diagram_figS2.R, README.md. There is no Python source for the Tesseract OCR stage, the U-Net(ResNet34) pod detector, the DeepLabV3 background segmenter, the geometric trait extractor or the 5-checkpoint seed-count ensemble, and no trained model weights or checkpoints. The deep-learning component that generates every image-based phenotype in the paper is unavailable.
gaps.how_to_close: Deposit the Python/PyTorch pipeline source, the training and inference configuration (learning rate, optimizer, epochs, batch size, augmentation policy, train/validation split, RNG seeds, segmentation threshold), and the trained checkpoints (including the 5 ensemble checkpoints from epochs 5-9) in the same repository or an archived Zenodo record.

gaps.where: Input imagery and annotations for steps C1-C5 (Data Availability statement)
gaps.missing: The 2,418 scanned pod images (4299x3035 px, 24-bit JPEG, 300 dpi), the LabelMe pod-segmentation training annotations, and the 1,678 manually red-dot-annotated seed-position images are not deposited in any repository or accession. Only derived per-genotype phenotypes ('raw phenotypic data ... BLUEs and BLUPs') are provided, as supplementary files. The image pipeline therefore has no runnable input at all.
gaps.how_to_close: Deposit the scanned image set and both annotation sets (with the plot/genotype identifier mapping) in a public archive such as Zenodo, Figshare or CyVerse, and cite the DOI in the Data Availability statement.

gaps.where: Whole analysis environment (both the Python/PyTorch stack and the R stack)
gaps.missing: No environment lockfile, container image digest, conda environment.yml, renv.lock or requirements.txt exists in the repository or is claimed in the prose. Pins are prose-only and partial: the paper gives Python 3.10, PyTorch 1.13, Tesseract v5.3.0, TASSEL v5.0, STRUCTURE v2.3.4, GAPIT v3, scikit-learn 1.3.0, SequenceServer v3.1.2, BLASTP 2.15.0; the README adds R >= 4.2.0 (a floating lower bound, not a pin) with GAPIT3 v3.1.0, rrBLUP v4.6.1, sommer v4.3.3, lme4 v1.1-34, data.table v1.14.8, ggplot2 v3.4.2, dplyr v1.1.2. segmentation_models_pytorch, OpenCV, Albumentations, corrplot, inti, qqman, ggrepel, ggpubr, STRUCTURE HARVESTER and CLUMPAK carry no version at all, and the CUDA/cuDNN stack behind 'All models ran on NVIDIA GPUs' is unstated. Version is therefore capped at 1 for every step that is pinned at all.
gaps.how_to_close: Ship a conda-lock/pixi.lock covering the Python side and an renv.lock covering the R side (or a container image referenced by digest), declare the target platform and the CUDA/cuDNN versions, and replace 'R version 4.2.0 or later' with the exact R version used.

gaps.where: GWAS/GP genotypic input (README 'Data Linkage' section vs. paper Data Availability statement)
gaps.missing: The two documents disagree about where the genotype matrix lives and neither resolves to a downloadable SNP dataset. The paper points to Legume Information System accession VC1973A.gnm7.SB53 (https://data.legumeinfo.org/Vigna/radiata/genomes/VC1973A.gnm7.SB53/), which is a reference-genome assembly directory rather than the 13,414-SNP GBS genotype matrix used for LD, STRUCTURE, GWAS and rrBLUP. The README instead states the GWAS and genomic-prediction scripts consume 'the genotypic dataset (available on Figshare)', but no Figshare DOI, URL or accession appears in the README, the paper, or the repository. The specific HapMap file with 13,414 filtered SNPs for the 372-genotype panel is not retrievable from either pointer.
gaps.how_to_close: Deposit the filtered 13,414-SNP HapMap/VCF file (and the upstream 19,658-SNP file) under a citable DOI and reference that exact DOI in both the Data Availability statement and the README, replacing the bare 'available on Figshare' phrasing.

gaps.where: Repository versioning — github.com/vboddepalli89/Image-based-pod-phenotyping (created 2025-10-20, last pushed 2026-04-01, 8 blobs, no license)
gaps.missing: The repository has no releases and no tags, and neither the paper nor the README cites a commit SHA, so there is no way to identify the code state that produced this preprint's results. This is not hypothetical drift: the README already describes a materially different, later version of the study — a T2T 'Weilv-9' reference genome, 65 significant SNPs, and candidate genes on chromosomes 4 and 6, conditionally accepted in G3 — whereas this preprint reports 45 significant SNPs, LIS accession VC1973A.gnm7.SB53, and candidate genes Vradi01g00001116 (chromosome 1) and Vradi02g00003971 (chromosome 2). The code currently on the default branch is therefore probably not the code behind this preprint. The repository also carries no license, so reuse rights are undefined.
gaps.how_to_close: Cut a tagged release (or archive to Zenodo for a versioned DOI) corresponding to the preprint analyses, cite that tag/DOI in the paper, and add a LICENSE file.

gaps.where: Version pinning for steps C13 (SVEN) and C15 (BLASTP / LIS JBrowse / TAIR)
gaps.missing: SVEN is cited only by reference (Li et al. 2023) with no package name, version, prior specification, screening threshold, MCMC length or RNG seed. The candidate-gene BLASTP is given no version and the LIS/TAIR protein databases no release or access date. Both steps cap at NI on the version axis alone.
gaps.how_to_close: Name and pin the SVEN implementation and record its full model settings and seed; record the BLAST+ version and the LIS/TAIR database release identifiers and access dates.

gaps.where: Stochastic steps without recorded seeds — C2/C3/C5 (network training and checkpoint ensembling), C9 (STRUCTURE MCMC, 5 runs per K), C13 (SVEN Bayesian sampling), C17 (10-fold cross-validation partitioning)
gaps.missing: No RNG seed is reported for any stochastic step. STRUCTURE's 5 independent runs per K, the SVEN sampler, the random assignment of 372 genotypes into ten CV subsets, and all network weight initialisation and data-order shuffling are unseeded in the prose, so exact numerical reproduction of the reported prediction accuracies (0.61-0.85), the delta-K optimum and the SNP sets is not achievable — only distributional agreement.
gaps.how_to_close: Publish fixed seeds (and the exact CV fold assignments, which the paper says were held identical across phenotyping methods) alongside the scripts.

gaps.where: Phenotypic inputs and analysis outputs (README 'Data Linkage' section)
gaps.missing: Every repository script is wired to manuscript supplementary tables rather than to files in the repository: scripts 01-03 require Supplemental Table 1, scripts 04-05 require Supplemental Table 3, script 06 requires Supplemental Table 5, and outputs are asserted to be Supplemental Tables 4, 6 and 7. The repository contains no data directory, so nothing runs without first locating and reformatting bioRxiv supplementary spreadsheets, whose exact column layout is not documented.
gaps.how_to_close: Include the input tables (or a fetch script with checksums) in the repository under a data/ directory, and document the expected column schema for each script.

gaps.where: Manual seed annotation step (wet-lab/manual, W) and, indirectly, the C5 training data
gaps.missing: Seed-position annotation of 1,678 images was performed with Microsoft Paint on Windows 10 — proprietary, GUI-driven, and unscriptable. The annotation procedure ('the left side ten pods were annotated with red dots ... based on the seed position', results recorded in an Excel sheet) has no machine-readable specification.
gaps.how_to_close: Release the resulting annotation files in an open format (COCO/PNG masks/CSV of coordinates) so the annotation tool choice becomes irrelevant to reproduction.

gaps.where: Steps C15 and C16 — hosted interactive services
gaps.missing: Candidate-gene identification and the synteny chord diagram were produced through hosted web interfaces (Legume Information System JBrowse/ZZBrowse/Genome Context Viewer/Gene Family Search at legumeinfo.org, TAIR BLAST at arabidopsis.org, SequenceServer v3.1.2 at sequenceserver.legumeinfo.org). There is no script, no query log, no downloaded database snapshot and no access date, so these steps depend on the live state of third-party servers whose contents change without notice.
gaps.how_to_close: Record the query sequences, exact parameters and access dates, archive the retrieved database subsets, and provide a local BLAST+ command line reproducing the search.

gaps.missing: The 2022-23 RCBD field trials of the 372-genotype IMD panel at Iowa State University AEA (Boone, Iowa) and the Burkey and Bruner farms, R6-stage harvesting and pod bagging, RGB image acquisition on an Epson Expression 11000 XL scanner at 300 dpi with a colour calibration chart on a blue background, manual pod length/seed-count/curvature phenotyping, and manual seed annotation are physical/manual data-generation steps, out of scope for computational reproduction; counted in W (5) and not verdicted.
gaps.how_to_close: N/A for Tier-1 computational readiness. The reproducible entry point would be the deposited scan images (currently missing, see gap type 1) plus the supplementary phenotype tables.
